paper_title: SepLLM Accelerate Large Language Models by Compressing One Segment into   One Separator
caption: The evolution of KV caches in the streaming setting.
model_annotation:
The plot illustrates the evolution of key-value (KV) cache sizes over time in a streaming inference setting for large language models, as described in the paper “SepLLM: Accelerate Large Language Models by Compressing One Segment into One Separator.” The top panel shows the cumulative number of tokens processed (π) on the y-axis versus the number of tokens processed so far (m) on the x-axis, which spans from 0 to m₀ and beyond. The y-axis is linear and ranges from 0 to c−a, with horizontal dashed lines marking thresholds at w, c−a−s, and c−a. The plot features a sawtooth pattern: π increases linearly with slope 1 until it reaches c−a, then drops sharply to w, and repeats. At m = m₀, the line drops to w + a + s (as indicated by the dotted vertical line connecting to the bottom panel), suggesting a reset or compression event.

The bottom panel plots the size of the running KV cache (Size_run) on the y-axis against the same x-axis (m). The y-axis is linear, ranging from 0 to c, with horizontal dashed lines at w + a + s and c. The Size_run line also follows a sawtooth pattern: it increases linearly from 0 to c, then drops to w + a + s, and repeats. At m = m₀, the cache size drops from c to w + a + s, aligning with the reset point in the top plot. Both plots use solid black lines with sharp vertical drops and linear upward ramps, visually representing periodic compression of the KV cache to maintain bounded memory usage during streaming inference. The parameter s likely represents the size of a separator token or compressed segment, and a and w are offsets or buffer sizes related to the compression mechanism.
